Subject: Private deployment pricing questions and platform fee amortization

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Strato Health is very interested in a private VPC deployment for our clinical inference workloads. Before we move into procurement, a couple of commercial questions from my side:

1) Platform fee amortization — we'd prefer to amortize the platform fee over 24 months rather than a single up-front payment. Is that something Redwood can do for our pilot?
2) Anchor credit — if we commit to a 24-month starter commit and reference deployment, can you provide an anchor credit against the platform fee?
3) SLA swap — we have an internal constraint where we can accept a lower uptime SLO in exchange for a reduced platform fee during our pilot. Would Redwood entertain an SLA-tier swap in the term sheet?

I've attached our standard security questionnaire and procurement intake form to this thread (Security_Questionnaire.pdf). Victor from procurement is copied.

Goal: get a commercial outline we can show finance this week.

Best,
Alicia Moreno
Sr. Product Operations
Strato Health

Alicia — thanks for the clear ask and for the questionnaire. Short answers up front, then a proposal:

- Amortization: yes, we can amortize the platform fee over 24 months for pilot-to-production deals. We typically include a small financing spread for amortization; I'll outline options below.
- Anchor credit: we can provide an anchor credit that reduces the platform fee in year 1 when a minimum commit is signed.
- SLA swap: we can offer a tiered SLA swap where you accept a 99.7% SLO during pilot in exchange for a 10% reduction to the platform fee; we can make the reduction timebound and tied to pilot acceptance criteria.

Proposed commercial outline (high-level):
- Starter commit: $350k/year equivalent (24mo) with a 12-month front-weighted commit window for usage.
- Anchor credit: 12% one-time credit against the platform fee applied in month 1 on execution.
- Amortization: platform fee can be paid monthly over 24 months with a 2% annual financing spread (we can present alternative amortization structures if needed).
- SLA swap: during the pilot (first 90 days), Redwood will accept 99.7% SLO with a 10% fee reduction. If production goes live earlier than 90 days and meets acceptance criteria, the reduction ends.

Next steps: I'll attach a draft term sheet and loop in Ben (sales lead) and Marissa (CS/solutions) for implementation tasks. Can you confirm procurement timeline?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Kimberly / team — a few quick internal notes before we finalize the draft: 

1) Anchor credit math: 12% of platform fee for Year 1 looks sustainable for a $700k ARR equivalent deal. If Strato wants a 24% credit we need a higher commit or multi-account expansion guarantee.
2) Amortization risk: if we allow monthly amortization over 24 months we should put in a shortfall clause tied to usage (min monthly consumption). Suggest a 60% utilization floor in the SOW to avoid open credit exposure.
3) SLA swap guardrails: make the 99.7% swap strictly timeboxed to the pilot and require a set of acceptance tests (latency tail at P95/P99 under sample load) to flip back to standard SLO. Also add automatic rollback to hosted variant if on-prem doesn't meet stability thresholds for 14 consecutive days.

I'll also flag this to Finance for the amortization treatment; we may need legal to sign off on the shortfall clause language.

Ben
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Victor / Alicia — appreciate the fast turnaround. Final clarifications and concessions from Redwood below: 

1) Anchor credit pro rata: yes — the 12% anchor credit will be applied pro rata against the platform fee as you scale. If you exceed the starter commit by 25% within the first 6 months, we'll re-evaluate and can ladder an additional 4% credit (to a total of 16%), subject to a modest expansion confirmation.
2) Amortization + lockbox: we can support 24-month monthly amortization. For license continuity, Redwood will include a contractual assurance and an HSM-backed key escrow option; we cannot escrow the runtime artifacts but will provide a runbook and export of model weights metadata for portability under the agreed-upon terms.
3) Shortfall clause: we accept Ben's recommended shortfall protection language but will soften the utilization floor to 50% for the pilot phase only, with clear remediation steps before credit recoupment.
4) SLA swap mechanics: pilot SLO at 99.7% with a 10% fee reduction, timeboxed to pilot acceptance milestones Marissa outlined. If the on-prem environment misses the stability guardrail for 14 consecutive days, Redwood will enact an automated failover plan; credits are capped at 3 months of platform fee.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll update the draft term sheet with the pro rata anchor credit clause, amortization schedule, and the softened shortfall clause.
- Ben/legal to prepare redline-friendly language for the procurement team.
- Schedule a 30-minute sync Thursday 10:00 AM PT (please confirm).

If that timeline works, we'll route the updated term sheet and a short SOW addendum to your legal team by Thursday EOD.
